title: Geo-anchoring circuit-breaker and residency evidence export for Private/VPC
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem:
Teams deploying Redwood Private into customer VPCs and on-prem clusters currently have limited guardrails to prevent cross-region data egress during control-plane or node-level outages. In several design reviews we identified gaps: we lack an automatic enforcement mechanism that can circuit-break cross-region requests when a residency policy is violated, and we do not have a compact, verifiable export format for residency evidence that can be consumed by compliance teams or customers.

Goals:
1) Implement a geo-anchoring circuit-breaker: a runtime policy layer that asserts the allowed execution region(s) for a tenant and automatically rejects or quarantine requests that would be routed outside those regions during incident conditions.
2) Provide an evidence export (forensic bundle) that contains signed residency attestations, recent routing decisions, KV cache location metadata, and configuration snapshots for a configurable window (e.g., last 7 days). The bundle must be tamper-evident and suitable for audit ingestion.
3) Ensure the system integrates with Private/VPC control planes, supports operator overrides with an auditable approval flow, and can be toggled per-tenant.

Constraints and trade-offs considered:
- Strict enforcement (hard block) vs soft enforcement (reject with fallback): hard blocks give stronger guarantees but risk availability for customers with transient routing issues. We will implement a configurable policy mode (block | quarantine | warn) and default to quarantine for first rollout.
- Evidence fidelity vs size/cost: full trace exports are heavy. We will record a compressed, signed index plus sampled request traces for high-risk tenants.
- On-prem limitations: not all on-prem customers will have outbound access to our control plane. Evidence export must work locally (signed by local KMS/HSM) and be importable into central audit tools.

Design overview:
- Policy Store: extend residency policy model to include anchoring rules (allowed regions, max-latency boundaries, sandbox exceptions) and enforcement mode. Policies are versioned.
- Policy Enforcer (runtime): small GRPC sidecar run alongside serving nodes that validates route decisions against the policy and triggers a circuit-breaker state machine when violations exceed thresholds. Circuit-breaker states: CLOSED (normal), OPEN (reject/reroute/quarantine), HALF_OPEN (probing).
- Evidence Exporter: scheduled job (operator or API-triggered) that collects signed attestations from the policy store, routing logs (index + sampled traces), KV cache region metadata, and a canonical configuration snapshot. The job packages artifacts into a gzipped tar with a signature and an overall manifest.json.
- Audit and Approval Flow: for operator overrides we add a small service to record override requests, approvals (SAML/SSO), and TTLs. Overrides are included in the exported evidence.

Acceptance criteria:
- Policy schema updated and documented (console + API) with anchoring fields and enforcement modes.
- Circuit-breaker sidecar integrated into dedicated/private deployment template; deployment smoke test that simulates cross-region misrouting causes expected state transitions.
- Evidence export produces a signed artifact with manifest and can be validated independently (script in repo).
- Telemetry: metrics for policy violations, circuit-breaker state changes, export success/failure, and evidence bundle validation errors. Dashboards built in Console-2025.03 release.
- Integration tests cover operator override flow and local-only evidence signing (simulate offline control plane).

Rollout plan:
1) Feature flag behind tenant-level toggle; default enforcement mode set to quarantine.
2) Deploy sidecar to staging dedicated/private clusters and run canary tests with synthetic misrouting.
3) Enable evidence exporter for internal compliance tenants and validate artifacts.
4) Gradual opt-in for customers with communications and runbook updates.

Telemetry and observability:
- New metrics: residency.policy_violation_count, residency.circuit_breaker_state{state}, residency.evidence_export_duration_seconds, residency.evidence_export_validation_failures.
- Logs: sidecar emits structured events for policy evaluation with sampling to avoid high-cardinality explosion.
- Traces: sampled traces for export bundles.

Security and compliance notes:
- All exported bundles must be signed with tenant-scoped keys; for Private on-prem deployments use local KMS/HSM.
- Evidence manifests must include hashes of included files and the public key fingerprint used for signing.
- We will run security review before GA; see security_review_required flag.

Deliverables:
- API changes: residency policy schema, policy CRUD endpoints, evidence export endpoints.
- Runtime: circuit-breaker sidecar binary, deployment manifests, tests.
- Exporter: export job, validation script, and console link to retrieve bundles.
- Runbooks and user docs for compliance teams and operators.

2025-02-24 - Design review: added enforcement modes (block/quarantine/warn). PM requests operator-override audit trail. See design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RES/Geo+Anchoring+Design
2025-02-28 - Eng update: prototype sidecar implemented (branch: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/tree/feature/geo-anchoring). Basic policy eval passes unit tests.

2025-03-04 - QA: evidence export produced sample bundle and validation script; found timestamp normalization bug when control plane timezone differs. Patch in review: PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/8912
